chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ismail ibn Marrar, from Yunus, from Ali ibn Yaqteen, who said:
I asked Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him) about shortening (the prayer) in Makkah, so he said: 'Complete it, and it is not obligatory, except that I love for you what I love for myself.'

key_terms.التَّقْصِيرِ: Shortening the prayer (performing 2 rak'ahs instead of 4)
key_terms.مَكَّةَ: Makkah, the city of the Grand Mosque

ai.seo_question: Should prayers be shortened or completed in Makkah according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the ruling of *qasr* (shortening prayer) in Mecca, stating that while it is not obligatory to shorten it, he personally prefers performing the full prayer (*tamm*). This reflects the Shia scholarly view that the Prophet’s practice in Mecca was to pray fully, and the Imam’s recommendation aligns with this Sunnah, distinguishing between legal obligation (*wajib*) and preferred practice (*mustahabb*). The narration highlights the importance of following the Imam’s personal preference as a guide for believers in matters of ritual excellence.
